title: test(app-shell): a walled catalog-package install, upgrade or uninstall refusal reaches the operator with its posture-naming reason (objectui#7611 item 2)
body:
Part of #7611
Clause-②: no

This PR covers item 2 of the card's release record (comment 6158162134) and nothing else: package install, upgrade and uninstall under a wall, in the console. The card stays open for items 1, 3 and 4. The seat's claim is comment 6158502886.

## Result

The console already shows the walled refusal's reason on every path that can receive it. The release record called this "not measured", so I measured it first. Each install, upgrade and uninstall gesture shows the door's posture-naming sentence verbatim. **The PR is pins only.** No source file changes, and the changeset has empty frontmatter.

## The refusal's wire shape, read at objectstack `4806b18aea`

objectstack W2 (objectstack-ai/objectstack#22935, merge `4806b18aea`, carried by `@objectstack/*` `18.0.0-next.0`) refuses two things below the platform-operator rung under `group` / `isolated`: an install or upgrade of a package that carries security catalog items, and the uninstall of such a package.

**install-local** (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `refuseWalledCatalogPackage`) refuses on two requests:
- `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`, for an install and also an upgrade, with VERB `Installing`;
- `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/MANIFEST_ID`, for an uninstall, with VERB `Uninstalling`.

```text
403
{ "success": false,
  "error": { "code": "FORBIDDEN",
             "message": "VERB \"MANIFEST_ID\" is refused: the package carries security catalog items. VERDICT",
             "details": { "manifestId": "MANIFEST_ID", "catalogItems": [ { "type": "TYPE", "name": "NAME" } ] } } }
```

**`DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id`** (`@objectstack/runtime`, `refuseWalledCatalogPackageDelete`) answers through the dispatcher's `deps.error(message, 403)`, so `buildApiError` derives the code from the status (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`):

```text
403
{ "success": false,
  "error": { "code": "PERMISSION_DENIED",
             "message": "Deleting package \"PACKAGE_ID\" is refused: the package carries security catalog items. VERDICT",
             "httpStatus": 403 } }
```

VERDICT is the sentence from `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`). It is written for the first catalog type the package declares, checked in this order: position, permission set, capability. For example:

> Creating, changing or deleting a permission set requires the platform operator: this deployment runs the 'group' tenancy posture, where the security catalog is shared by every organization (ADR-0131 D3). Holding the `manage_metadata` capability inside an organization does not admit it. An organization's administrators assign the catalog's positions and permission sets to their own members instead.

**No posture field.** Neither envelope carries one. The posture appears only in the message. An upgrade goes to the same door as an install: the door checks both the incoming and the installed manifest, and answers with the `Installing` sentence.

## The console's paths, measured

Each case renders the real component. A stubbed `fetch` answers a real `Response` carrying the exact envelope above, with status text `Forbidden`. Each case runs under both `group` and `isolated`. `marketplaceApi` is not mocked.

| Gesture | Console path | Request | What the operator reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| install | package page, Install (`installLocal`) | `POST install-local` | the door's sentence, verbatim |
| upgrade | package page, Reinstall over an installed older version (3.2.0, latest 4.0.1) | `POST install-local`: no version is named, so the door installs `latest` over the installed one | the door's sentence, verbatim |
| uninstall | package page, local menu, Uninstall from runtime (`uninstallLocal`) | `DELETE install-local/MANIFEST_ID` | the door's sentence, verbatim |
| uninstall | Installed Apps, the row's Uninstall (`uninstallLocal`) | same | the door's sentence, verbatim; the row stays |
| install | catalog page, Your organization, Install (`installLocal` with `versionId: 'latest'`) | `POST install-local` | the door's sentence, verbatim |
| delete | Packages page, package sheet, Delete app (`apiJson`) | `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` | the door's sentence plus ` (PERMISSION_DENIED)` |
| install | Packages page, Import (`apiJson`, manifest inline) | `POST install-local` | the door's sentence plus ` (FORBIDDEN)` |

None of the five marketplace cases shows `Forbidden`, `HTTP_403` or a bare `FORBIDDEN`. Neither Packages page case shows `Forbidden` or this page's own fallback, `Request failed (403)`. The marketplace pins assert that each gesture's success sentence is absent, and that each request left the browser with the expected method, path and body.

**The `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` path (Zone 2, item 3).** The console calls it from one place: `PackageDetailSheet`'s Delete app on the Packages page (`views/metadata-admin`). That page also has a second door into install-local: Import, which posts the file's manifest inline. Both sit outside the claimed `console/marketplace/` surface. Both are measured here in one new test file beside the page, and no source there changes.

**Wording (Zone 2, item 4): verbatim, the existing convention.** Three reasons:
- **It is the convention.** `doInstallLocal` already shows the install-mode refusals as sent ("each message names its own remedy, and the page has nothing to add to it"). Both uninstall callers show `e.message`. The Packages page shows the envelope through `readEnvelopeFailureText`.
- **It reads well for a tenant admin.** The sentence names the action and the package, the reason (security catalog items), the posture, who may do it (the platform operator), that the admin's own `manage_metadata` does not admit it, and what they can do instead.
- **Localizing would need a server contract the console does not have.** The install-local refusal shares its code, `403 FORBIDDEN`, with the same door's missing-capability refusal, which ends ``requires the `manage_metadata` capability.``. The `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` refusal carries only the status-derived `PERMISSION_DENIED`. So the console could tell a walled refusal apart only by parsing the server's prose. That is a second reading of the refusal, and the server's own sentence already does the job.

## Tests

All runs are at head `ef8ab4ae4`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.walledCatalogRefusal-7611.test.tsx` → `Test Files  34 passed (34)`, `Tests  229 passed (229)`. That is the 32 existing marketplace suites, plus the new marketplace pin (11 tests) and the new Packages page pin (4 tests).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` and exits 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists both new test files.
- Build of the dependency closure, `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`: exit 0. All 29 packages were cache hits.
- eslint, as a proven narrowing. First, the population comes from eslint's own config: `--print-config` on a new file resolves 119 rules, so the file is linted, and the changeset `.md` matches no `files` glob. Second, `--format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings, both from the repo root with `--no-inline-config` and from `packages/app-shell`, the way its `lint` script runs. Third, untouched files are unaffected: the resolved config has `parserOptions.project` and `projectService` unset, so linting is not type-aware, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. The diff adds two files and edits none, so it cannot change any other file's lint result.
- Repo checks, all exit 0: `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (the changeset has empty frontmatter, which this gate accepts as a complete answer), `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:test-path-roots`, `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers`. Also derived from the workflows and run: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-lint-coverage`, `check-type-check-coverage`, and `pnpm check:` `unreferenced-sources` / `esm-specifiers` / `metadata-write-doors` / `handler-key-reads` / `self-import` / `i18n-keys` / `phantom-deps`.
- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins`. It exits 2 because there is no console build to read. It reads bundle-time registrations, and this diff ships no code.

**Ablation (one leg, on the committed tree):** run with objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. It replaced `readApiError`'s `payload?.error?.message   // the declared envelope` with `undefined`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0, and the blob from `4fd74da91c1c` to `922b64be38e3`. The marketplace pin then ran at `Tests  10 failed | 1 passed (11)`, which is the direction predicted beforehand. Each failure was `Unable to find an element with the text: Installing "com.example.crm" is refused: …`, with the page showing the bare `FORBIDDEN`: the exact shape of a dropped reason. The one pass is the harness CONTROL, which shows a bare form either way. The restore was proven: the blob after restore equals HEAD (`4fd74da91c1c`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the marker count is 0.

## Acceptance notes

These are observations only. None is filed, and none has a carrier.
- `uninstallLocal` throws an `Error` with neither `code` nor `status`, while `installLocal` carries both. Both of its callers show only `e.message`, so nothing user-visible depends on it today.
- The install-local 403 lists the declared items in `details.catalogItems`. The console does not show them. The sentence already says the package carries security catalog items, so listing the items would be a feature request, not part of this item.
- CI: `Spec Main Shape Gate` is red on `main` and on every PR (advisory, owned by objectui#12325). `OAuthConsentPage.public-client-12301` is a known timing flake (objectui#12344).

Files: `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/__tests__/walledCatalogPackageRefusal-7611.test.tsx`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.walledCatalogRefusal-7611.test.tsx`, `.changeset/7611-walled-package-refusal.md`.
